themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 344% increase—suggesting either a newly identified contamination source or emerging public awareness of lead hazards in Throgs Neck/Co-op City housing stock.
evidence: 5 lead complaints filed this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.68)
Recurring CB budget request to 'address illegal conversions and uses of buildings' (DOB) suggests older building stock vulnerability
reporting_angles: Investigate specific buildings or blocks where lead complaints clustered this week; interview residents about water, paint, soil testing
Examine whether new City testing initiative, school screening, or tenant advocacy group activity triggered complaint surge

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and facility complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 40 last week from a baseline of 4.1 per week—an 870% spike (z-score: 11.28, highest severity)—indicating widespread infrastructure or building system failures across the district in the past 7 days.
evidence: 40 complaints last week vs. 4.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.28, highest severity score)
870% increase marks most extreme statistical anomaly in dataset
Concurrent 773 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days suggests heating/cooling systems may be part of complaint cluster
reporting_angles: Map maintenance complaints by building or block; determine if Co-op City (largest co-op in US) or NYCHA buildings are driving spike
Identify what infrastructure failures are most common: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, structural; interview building superintendents and property managers
Cross-reference with DOB permit data: are 233 alteration permits under way masking underlying maintenance crises?

themes_detail.label: Unlicensed food vendors surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 4 last week from a 0.2 weekly baseline—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—suggesting either aggressive unlicensed vendor activity or increased enforcement/reporting in the past 7 days.
evidence: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66, second-highest severity)
1500% spike is sharpest percentage increase after maintenance complaints
Suggests emerging permitting or enforcement issue or new vendor encroachment near transit hubs, parks, or schools
reporting_angles: Survey high-foot-traffic areas (Co-op City retail, transit nodes, Pelham Bay Park) for unlicensed vendors; document locations and patterns
Interview DOHMH and SBS about whether new complaint reporting mechanism or enforcement blitz triggered spike

themes_detail.label: Rodent and animal complaints rise
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 4 over 2 weeks ago from a 1.0 weekly baseline (300% increase, z-score: 4.24), and animal-in-park complaints spiked to 3 three weeks ago (700% increase, z-score: 3.77), suggesting environmental conditions or seasonal pressures attracting wildlife to residential and park areas.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.24)
3 animal-in-park complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77)
Concurrent 'unsanitary condition' complaints (232 over 90 days) and illegal dumping (218) suggest food waste accumulation
reporting_angles: Investigate whether sanitation pickup delays, illegal dumping hotspots, or park maintenance gaps are creating pest habitat
Interview residents in Co-op City and neighborhoods near Pelham Bay Park about wildlife sightings and health impacts

themes_detail.label: Tree die-off and environmental decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 9 two weeks ago from a 1.5 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score: 4.74), and litter basket complaints peaked at 3 three weeks ago (700% spike, z-score: 5.42), signaling environmental neglect or possible drought/disease event affecting green space.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.74)
3 litter basket complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
Recurring CB budget request for 'reconstruct or upgrade building in a park' suggests parks maintenance is chronic issue
reporting_angles: Survey Pelham Bay Park, local greenways, and street trees for disease, drought stress, or pest damage; photograph affected areas
Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance schedule and budget constraints in CD 210; cross-reference with CB requests
